metaDesc: Where locals eat mookata and BBQ buffet in Phayao, Thailand — from Fah Sai and Kin Keng to 17Grill and the lakeside spots. Real reviews, prices and hours.
keywords: Phayao mookata, Phayao buffet, Phayao BBQ buffet, mookata restaurants Phayao, lakeside mookata Phayao
intro: Once the heat eases off in Phayao, the dinner locals meet up for most is mookata — the dome grill where you sear meat on top and dip-cook in the broth around it, then sit and talk for hours. A couple of hundred baht is enough to leave full. We picked the spots with real reviews behind them: places in town, the ones outside the university, and a few by the lake that throw in a view.

blocks.html: Most mookata in Phayao is a single-price buffet — sit and eat as much as you like — ranging from old-school charcoal grills to electric ones in air-conditioned rooms. The common ground almost everywhere is marinated pork, pork belly, grilled offal, meatballs, fresh vegetables, noodles, and a corner of desserts and ice cream. What sets places apart is how fresh the ingredients are, the dipping sauces, and the setting. We've ranked them by the popularity and value people in Phayao bring up most.

items.name: Fah Sai Mookata Phayao
items.blurb: An in-town buffet spot people in Phayao talk about a lot. The strength is the marinated pork done in several recipes, plus a self-serve spread of fried items, salad, desserts and fresh fruit. Hot grill, fresh ingredients — a great pick for coming as a group.
items.meta: In Phayao town · Wiang subdistrict · dinner only

items.name: Kin Keng Mookata Buffet, Phayao branch
items.blurb: A mookata-buffet chain people in the North know by name, and the Phayao branch reviews well. Everything's laid out buffet-line style so it's easy to grab, and the marinated pork is well balanced. Good for a family or a big group.

items.name: 17Grill Phayao
items.blurb: A newer spot doing a beef-grill and seafood buffet — beef, pork, prawns, squid, sushi, marinated raw prawns, and ice-cream bars. Dips include jaew, suki and seafood sauce. It's on the Chamchuri corner, between the kindergarten and the way to Gateway Hotel.

items.name: Mahaniyom Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: A single-price buffet the province has highlighted before. The basics are all here — pork, offal, meatballs, vegetables, noodles and dessert — so it suits big eaters who still want to keep the budget in check.

items.name: Rim Kwan Mookata, Seafood & Chinese Hot Pot Buffet
items.blurb: A lakeside spot where you get mookata, seafood and Chinese hot pot all in one place, drinks included in the buffet price. The open setting near the water makes it a good one for a long, easy evening.

items.name: Lam Him Kwan Mookata, Seafood & Jim Jum Buffet
items.blurb: Another lakeside spot that puts mookata, seafood and jim jum together — your call whether to grill or dip-cook. The lake view at sunset is the extra a lot of people come for.

items.name: Phai Daeng Mookata
items.blurb: A buffet with a big spread and friendly prices, and no time limit on your table. Good for a group of friends who want to sit and eat at their own pace.

items.name: Wara Shabu & Mookata
items.blurb: Stands out for its dipping sauces — several to choose from, including seafood, jaew and two suki recipes. You can do both shabu and mookata, so it's a fit for anyone who likes a punchy dip.

items.name: Mu Sam Chan Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: An evening buffet that leans on fresh, clean ingredients and punchy dipping sauces, with a low starting price. Good for a couple or a small group who just want an easy meal.

items.name: Mookata spots outside University of Phayao (Mae Ka zone)
items.blurb: The area outside the University of Phayao around Mae Ka has several mookata and shabu buffets at student prices. The spread is modest but the value is real — good if you're on a tight budget and want a lively crowd.
items.meta: Mae Ka subdistrict · outside University of Phayao

blocks.title: How to pick a spot
blocks.html: If you're coming with a big group and want a view, go lakeside and book a table around sunset. If keeping the budget down matters more, the in-town spots and the Mae Ka zone start cheaper. Most open around 4–5pm and run late; weekends get busy, so aim to arrive before 7pm or call ahead to book.

blocks.text: What does it cost, and is it worth it

blocks.html: Most mookata buffets in Phayao sit in the ฿159–299 per person range. The university zone and the budget spots start around ฿159–199, while the in-town places with a big spread or the lakeside spots that add seafood and hot pot move up to ฿239–299. If you eat a lot and stay a while, the buffet beats ordering à la carte by a clear margin — and plenty of places have no time limit.

items: Light budget ฿159–199 — the Mae Ka zone outside the university, Phai Daeng, and Wara Shabu, good for keeping costs down and for student groups.
Mid ฿239–269 — Mahaniyom, 17Grill and Kin Keng, with a wider spread and seafood or beef added.
Worth it for the view ฿249–299 — Fah Sai, the Rim Kwan buffet and Lam Him Kwan, where you get a big spread or a lake view thrown in.
Start by rubbing pork fat over the dome to grease it, then lay down the marinated pork so it won't stick.
Grill or dip-cook offal and seafood until they're properly done, especially prawns and squid.
Keep separate tongs for raw and cooked food to cut the risk of an upset stomach.
Keep topping up the broth in the moat so you can blanch vegetables and noodles while the pork grills.
Save dessert and ice cream for the end, and take only what you'll finish so nothing goes to waste.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Prices and opening hours shift with the season and promotions, and some places charge for food you take but don't finish. Before you go, check the restaurant's page again or call to book a table on weekends to be sure.

faq.q: Which mookata in Phayao is the best value?
faq.a: For value, the spots outside University of Phayao around Mae Ka, plus Phai Daeng and Wara Shabu, start around ฿159–199 with no time limit — a modest spread but good value. If you want a big spread or a lake view, Fah Sai and the lakeside spots at around ฿249–299 are worth it in their own way.

faq.q: Roughly what does mookata cost in Phayao?
faq.a: Most are single-price buffets in the ฿159–299 per person range. Budget spots start around ฿159–199, while in-town places with a big spread or lakeside spots that add seafood and hot pot run around ฿239–299.

faq.q: Is there mookata by the lake in Phayao?
faq.a: Yes — places like the Rim Kwan mookata-seafood-Chinese-hot-pot buffet and Lam Him Kwan, where you get mookata, seafood and the lake view at sunset. Book a table for the evening, since people love coming to sit and watch the view.

faq.q: What time do mookata spots in Phayao open?
faq.a: Most open for dinner, starting around 4–5pm and running to 9 or 11pm depending on the place. Weekends get busy, so aim to arrive before 7pm or call ahead to book.

faq.q: Is mookata different from shabu in Phayao?
faq.a: At many places in Phayao it's a combined dome where you grill in the middle and dip-cook around the moat in one go — like Wara Shabu and the lakeside spots — so you can grill pork or dip shabu in the same meal.
